title: Tackling real-time hair-card bottlenecks: Where do DCC-to-engine handoffs usually break down for you?
author: abdalrohman97
selftext:
Hi technical artists — we’re building HairStorm, a standalone Windows application for creating hair cards for real-time characters. It isn’t a Blender or 3ds Max add-on.

The demo shows procedural strand layers, texture-map previews, UV card layout and grooming on a character: [https://youtu.be/XGCTxYX2nnc](https://youtu.be/XGCTxYX2nnc)

For people making characters in Blender, 3ds Max or a game engine: where does your hair-card pipeline get awkward — the atlas/UV handoff, shaping cards, or moving assets and materials into the target app? What export or shader details would you want to see explained in a follow-up?

Project website: [https://cgnas.com/hairstorm/](https://cgnas.com/hairstorm/)
